HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. Low wide shot across black water in a steam cavern at night. Far side of the pool, midground: Kim Yushin as an old man of seventy-nine, white hair and white beard, back straight again, standing at the edge of the steam in a plain deep-blue burial robe, hands at his sides, like a guest who arrived early, the water at his shins. Foreground right, large and soft-focused: the water goddess Hyullé, in a white silk jeogori and soaked cyan chima, sinking down into the water with her hand at her mouth, wet hair, eyes wide and wet. On a rock far left, a small out-of-focus figure of a woman in orange turned to face the cave wall. ONE device: a long pale streak of lamplight on the water running from Hyullé to Yushin like a path. Marshal blue #2A5FB8 as the catch on his robe; cyan #2eb8c4 in the drip off Hyullé. Yushin is painterly webtoon; Hyullé is the divine one, more realistic skin. No glow, no halo. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = yushin, SECOND face = hyulle. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_cave (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), binyeo board hyulle (her hair ornament exactly; not clothing). KIM YUSHIN — Look: Tall, broad-shouldered, long black hair in a high topknot-ponytail with trailing Silla-blue cloth tails; level hard brows, deep-set eyes. Dress: Silla-blue po and trousers, plum-violet sash knotted at the waist, white inner collar, dark wrapped forearms. Off duty: plain blue po, no jewelry. Now: Old marshal: grey-streaked beard, heavier frame, slower — still stands, still counts. Colour #2A5FB8. HYULLÉ Colour #2eb8c4. PLACE Steam Cavern (골화천) — attached board /pl_cave.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Golhwacheon (골화천), the steam cavern hot spring: a dark pond under wet black stone, steam, motes in the element colors; everyone bathes IN the black water like a Korean public bath, bare bathing bodies, nothing on but water; generally dark, magical anime-painterly atmosphere, not a photoreal cave. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
